message.content:
Below are quick‑and‑dirty ways to pull down today’s date directly from your shell – either **Unix/Linux/macOS** (`bash`, `zsh`, …) or **Windows Command Prompt / PowerShell**.

---

### On *nix shells (Linux, macOS)

| What you type | Typical output format | Notes |
|---------------|-----------------------|-------|
| ```bash\n date \n``` | `Tue Apr 23 14:07:32 PDT 2022` | Default human‑readable form. |
| ```bash\n date +'%F' \n``` | `2022-04-23` | ISO 8601 style (`YYYY-MM-DD`). |
| ```bash\n date '+%A, %B %-d, %Y at %I:%M %p'\n``` | `Tuesday, April 23, 2022 at 02:07 PM` | Custom layout. |

*If you only care about the numeric day/month/year:*  
```bash
date +'${YEAR}-${MONTH}-${DAY}'
```
(you’ll still need to parse the fields).

#### Example session

```text
$ date
Tue Apr 23 14:07:32 PDT 2022
$ date +'%F'
2022-04-23
$ date '+%a %b %e %H:%M:%S %Z %Y'
Tue Apr 23 14:07:32 PDT 2022
```

---

### In Windows Command Prompt (cmd.exe)

| What you type | Typical output format | Notes |
|--------------|----------------------|-------|
| ```bat\n echo %DATE%\n``` | `4/23/22` | Locale dependent. Usually month/day/year. |
| ```bat\n echo %TIME%\n``` | `14:07:32.00` | Time part. |
| ```bat\n wmic path win32_localtime get DayOfWeek\,,Day,\Month,\Year /format:list\n``` | `Day=23\nMonth=Apr\nYear=2022\n...` | More granular pieces. |

To force a specific order you’d normally write a small batch script or rely on PowerShell instead.

#### Quick demo

```bat
C:\Users\User>echo %DATE%
4/23/22
C:\Users>User>echo %TIME%
14:07:32.00
```

---

### Using PowerShell (works on both Windows & recent macOS/Linux when installed)

PowerShell gives you rich objects out of the box:

```powershell
PS C:\> Get-Date          # full object
Monday, April 24, 2022 10:15:42 AM

PS C:\> Get-Date -Format yyyyMMdd   # formatted string
20220424

PS C:\> Get-Date -UFormat "%c"
Thu Apr 25 11:20:01 2022
```

Because PowerShell returns a `[DateTime]` object, you can do arithmetic too:

```powershell
(Get-Date).AddDays(-7).ToString('yyyy-MM-dd')
```

--- 

### TL;DR

| Platform | One‑liner for “today” |
|----------|------------------------|
| Bash/Zsh | `date +'%F'` → `2022-04-23` |
| Cmd.exe | `echo %DATE%` → locale‑dependent |
| PowerShell | `Get-Date -Format yyyyMMdd` → `20220423` |

Pick whichever fits your workflow!
